targets.authors: Pagel M., Atkinson Q.D., Meade A.
targets.title: Frequency of word-use predicts rates of lexical evolution throughout Indo-European history.
targets.evidence_quote: We have previously shown that the ‘low limit’ number words (from one to five) have exceptionally slow rates of lexical replacement when measured across the Indo-European languages. Here we replicate this finding within the Bantu and Austronesian language families, and with new data for the Indo-European languages.
targets.outcome_quote: Here we replicate this finding within the Bantu and Austronesian language families, and with new data for the Indo-European languages.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly describe replication of earlier low-limit number-word stability using new language datasets. Main results support unusually slow replacement across all three families. The study supplying each lexical dataset is not itself a target. Zipf provides explanatory context rather than a separately designated finding this paper sets out to retest.
